name: Blind & shade repair
title: Blind & Shade Repair in Los Angeles | John Crawford Co.
description: Blind and shade repair in Los Angeles. Share photos and describe the problem so John Crawford Company can review the product, available parts and repair options.
heading: Blind and shade repair in Los Angeles
intro: A blind that won’t tilt or a shade that stops halfway leaves you with less control over light and privacy. Tell us what’s happening, and we’ll help you find out whether the treatment can be repaired.

overview.heading: Start with the treatment you already have.
paragraphs: If you’re happy with the way a blind or shade looks, it’s worth finding out why it no longer works. The problem may be a small part, a control issue or wear that needs a closer look. A description and a few photos give us a useful starting point.

John has collected blind and shade components over years of installation and repair work. That experience helps him assess selected brands, including some products we didn’t originally supply. The next step depends on the treatment’s construction, condition and the parts available for it.

topics.title: A blind that won’t adjust
topics.text: Let us know whether the slats won’t tilt, the blind won’t lift or something has come loose. Describe what happens when you try to use it, even if you don’t know which part is causing the problem.

topics.title: A shade that catches or stops
topics.text: Tell us where the shade stops and whether it hangs unevenly. Photos of the whole window and the area giving you trouble help us understand the problem in context.

topics.title: A motorized shade that won’t respond
topics.text: Include the system name if you know it, the control you use and whether one shade or several are affected. Some issues can be addressed with phone guidance; others need inspection or parts.

feature.heading: A few photos help us understand the problem.
paragraphs: Start with a photo of the whole blind or shade, then add a closer view of the damaged or loose area. A manufacturer’s label can help identify the product. You can describe the problem in your own words; knowing the name of the mechanism isn’t necessary.
If you remember when and where you bought the treatment, include those details too. An approximate date is useful, and it’s fine to say that you don’t know the brand or age.

link.text: You can also email your photos

quote.text: John is Amazing! He is so kind and honest. Overall great guy to work with and helped me source blind brackets we had installed from Costco over 20 years ago! …
quote.author: Kamran Jahangard

questions_heading: Questions about blind and shade repairs

faqs.question: Can you repair blinds you didn’t sell?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. We can work on selected outside brands when suitable parts are available. Send photos and a description first so we can review the product. Similar-looking blinds may use different components, so we need to assess the treatment you have.

faqs.question: What if I don’t know the brand or how old it is?
faqs.answer: Send the details you do have. A photo of the whole treatment, any visible label and the problem area can help. An approximate purchase date or the name of the original seller is useful, but you can start the conversation without them.

faqs.question: Can you help with older blinds or shades?
faqs.answer: Age alone doesn’t tell us whether a repair is possible. The construction, condition and availability of suitable components matter. John has helped with older treatments, but each product needs to be reviewed on its own.

faqs.question: Can a motorized shade problem be resolved by phone?
faqs.answer: Some can. John has guided customers through an app adjustment when that was appropriate. Describe the system and what happens when you use the control, and we’ll work out whether phone guidance or an in-person check is the next step.

faqs.question: What if the treatment needs replacing?
faqs.answer: We can help you compare new blinds or shades. Tell us what you liked about the original treatment and what you’d change. A free in-home consultation includes samples and measuring for a replacement project.

contact_heading: Let’s find out what your blind or shade needs.
contact_text: Email John a few photos and a short description, or call to explain the problem. From Woodland Hills, we help customers across Los Angeles and nearby Valley communities find out whether a repair is possible.

details.heading: What makes a repair worth doing?

items.heading: The right parts.
paragraphs: Older treatments may use components that are difficult to find. John’s accumulated parts can help with some products; for others, we need to find out whether a suitable part can still be sourced.

items.heading: The condition of the treatment.
paragraphs: A broken part may be worth replacing if the rest of the blind or shade is in good condition. We also look for worn or brittle materials that could make a repair less worthwhile.

items.heading: The cost compared with replacement.
paragraphs: Parts and labor can make a repair more expensive than expected. If the work looks unlikely to last, or replacement is the better use of your budget, we’ll explain why and talk through your options.

name: Consultation & measuring
title: Free In-Home Consultation & Measuring | John Crawford Co.
description: Free in-home window treatment consultations in Los Angeles. We bring samples to your home, help you compare options and take measurements for your project.
heading: Free in-home consultation & measuring
intro: We come to your home with window treatment samples, take measurements and help you work through the choices in the rooms you’re furnishing. The consultation is free, whether you’re starting with one window or planning several rooms.

overview.heading: Compare the samples beside your own windows.
paragraphs: A fabric can look quite different beside your own windows. During the visit, you can compare it with the wall color, hold a finish next to existing woodwork and see how the material looks in the room’s daylight.

The visit also gives us a chance to understand what you want to change. Afternoon sun may be catching a television screen, a front room may need more privacy, or the windows may feel unfinished. We start with the way you use the room and work through the treatments that suit it.

topics.title: Light and privacy
topics.text: We’ll ask when the room is used and how much daylight you want to keep. A bedroom, home office and street-facing living room can call for different fabrics, linings or levels of coverage.

topics.title: Style and materials
topics.text: A woven texture, a tailored roller shade and soft drapery each change the room in a different way. Compare color, texture and finish with the furnishings you already have.

topics.title: Everyday control
topics.text: Consider the windows you adjust each day and the ones that are hard to reach. We can explain manual and compatible motorized options while you’re comparing styles, so you can choose how you’d like to operate them.

feature.heading: Measuring is included in the home visit.
paragraphs: We take the measurements for your project and look at the details around the opening: its depth, the trim, handles and nearby space. Those details help determine where a blind, shade or shutter can sit and how it will operate.
For drapery, the arrangement extends beyond the glass. We look at the position and span of the rod or track, how far the fabric will extend and where the panels will rest when open.

When you’re considering several windows together, we also look at how the treatments will relate to one another. You get help with the overall arrangement as well as the measurements for each opening.

story.heading: One window is welcome.
paragraphs: Early in his career in upstate New York, John drove about an hour to a customer who needed a single mini blind for her bathroom. That small job led to a referral for a whole house of blinds.
He still welcomes the smaller projects. A bathroom window, one room of shades or a set of drapery is enough reason to get in touch.

faqs.question: Is the in-home consultation free?
faqs.answer: Yes. The free visit includes bringing samples to your home, discussing your windows and taking measurements for your project. Contact us to arrange a time.

faqs.question: Do I need to choose a product before we meet?
faqs.answer: You can start with an idea, a few inspiration photos or something you want to change about the room. We’ll help you compare suitable treatments, materials and controls during the visit.

faqs.question: Should I measure the windows myself?
faqs.answer: We take the measurements needed for your project. Photos and a description of the windows can help start the conversation, but you don’t need a set of measurements to request a consultation.

faqs.question: Can we discuss motorized shades during the visit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell us which windows are difficult to reach and how you’d like to control the shades. We’ll review compatible products and controls, including any power or connection requirements that apply.

faqs.question: Can I visit the showroom instead?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our Woodland Hills showroom is available by appointment for comparing materials and finishes in person. You can call or use the appointment inquiry form to request a visit.

contact_heading: Let’s see the windows you have in mind.
contact_text: Tell us which rooms you’re considering and what you’d like to change. We’ll arrange a free in-home consultation, bring samples and take measurements. We serve Los Angeles and nearby Valley communities from our appointment-only Woodland Hills showroom.

details.heading: From the samples to your quote.

items.heading: Talk through the budget.
paragraphs: Your budget is part of the conversation. We compare treatment styles, materials and operating options, and explain how those choices affect the quote. If you’re considering one room now and others later, we can discuss the rooms you want to focus on.

items.heading: Plan the complete treatment.
paragraphs: We’ll explain the hardware, controls and installation involved with each option. That helps you compare the full cost of the treatments you’re considering.

items.heading: Understand the next step.
paragraphs: With the measurements and selections in place, we can prepare your quote and discuss product availability and installation. If an item is delayed or goes on backorder, we keep you informed about what has changed.

quote.text: It was a pleasure working with John Crawford Co. from ordering through installation. The process was seamless.
quote.author: monica fitzhugh

name: Installation
title: Window Treatment Installation Los Angeles | John Crawford
description: Careful measuring and professional installation for custom blinds, shades, shutters and drapery in Los Angeles. Start with a free in-home consultation.
heading: Window treatment installation in Los Angeles
intro: Even the most beautiful shade, shutter or blind needs to fit well to look right and work properly. Careful measuring and installation are among the most important parts of the job. Start with a free in-home consultation: we bring samples to your home and take measurements for your windows.

overview.heading: A good fit takes more than width and height.
paragraphs: John began installing window treatments in the mid-1980s, before opening his California store in 1995.

We measure the width at several points up the window and the height at several points across it. We also check whether the opening is square and level. One width and one height don’t tell the whole story.
Mounting depth, trim, handles and room for the treatment to move all matter too. Without the right fit, a treatment can look uneven or fail to open and close smoothly.

At installation, we check the mounting brackets, alignment and operation, as well as how the finished treatment looks in the window. With drapery, we also check how the fabric hangs and where the panels sit when open.

topics.title: Blinds and shades
topics.text: Mounting depth and the space around the window affect where a treatment sits. We check positioning and movement, including clearances around handles or trim that could interfere with everyday use.

topics.title: Shutters
topics.text: The fit involves both the frame and the panels. We check how the panels open and the louvers operate, with attention to nearby trim, handles and the space needed for access.

topics.title: Drapery and hardware
topics.text: The height and span of a rod or track shape the way drapery frames the window. We fit the hardware and check how the panels hang, travel and sit when open.

feature.heading: Motorized control that fits your routine.
paragraphs: With motorized shades, you can use a remote, a wall control or an app, depending on the system. We’ll help you compare the controls available for the shades you’re considering.

We set up the shades and controls, including any hub or gateway the system needs, and check that the shades respond correctly. If hardwired shades need an electrical connection, we can coordinate with your electrician.
We show you how to adjust the shades and answer your questions about the controls.

quote.text: Great service throughout entire process. From 1st consult to installation every step was performed professionally & with quality craftsmanship. Our shades & shutters are more beautiful than expected! …
quote.author: Mary Yingling

faqs.question: How do I get started?
faqs.answer: Request a free in-home consultation. We bring samples, measure your windows and help you work through the product and control choices. From there, we can prepare a quote and discuss installation.

faqs.question: Can you help with just one window?
faqs.answer: Yes. John welcomes one-window projects as well as work across several rooms. Tell us what you’re considering, and we’ll talk through the options.

faqs.question: Do you install drapery rods and tracks?
faqs.answer: We install drapery rods and tracks, check the mounting points and allow space for the fabric to open and close. We also check how the finished drapery hangs.

faqs.question: Can you help with motorized and hardwired shades?
faqs.answer: We install compatible motorized treatments and help with control and hub setup. If the arrangement requires electrical work, we can discuss coordination with your electrician.

faqs.question: How long will installation take?
faqs.answer: The time depends on the number of windows, treatment types and mounting details. Once we know your selections and the layout, we can discuss the work involved and the installation arrangements.

faqs.question: What if I have a question after installation?
faqs.answer: Call us and describe what is happening. We’ll help work out whether guidance by phone is appropriate or an in-person check is needed. Parts or repairs depend on the product and the problem.

contact_heading: Start with a free in-home consultation.
contact_text: Tell us which windows you’d like to cover. We’ll bring samples, take measurements and talk through the product choices and installation work.

details.heading: From the measuring visit to installation.

items.heading: Confirm the project details.
paragraphs: The measurements, product selections, hardware and controls need to work together. We review those details as part of the quote, including any mounting or power requirements that affect the installation. We’ll explain what’s involved and answer your questions.

items.heading: Discuss availability and timing.
paragraphs: A single blind and several rooms of motorized shades involve different amounts of work. We’ll discuss product availability and timing for your project, and keep you informed if an item is delayed.

items.heading: Stay in touch afterward.
paragraphs: John has talked customers through an app adjustment by phone when a shade stopped working as expected. Some questions can be resolved with guidance; others need an in-person check. Tell us what is happening, and we’ll discuss the next step.

name: Commercial window treatments
title: Commercial Window Treatments Los Angeles | John Crawford
description: Interior blinds and shades for Los Angeles offices, restaurants and businesses. Get help with glare, privacy, product selection, measuring and installation.
heading: Commercial window treatments in Los Angeles
intro: Daylight should work for the people using your space. We help Los Angeles offices, restaurants and businesses choose interior blinds and shades for screen glare, privacy and the look of the room, with measuring, installation and compatible motorized controls.

overview.heading: Plan around the way your business uses the room.
paragraphs: The windows nearest a workstation may need different coverage from those beside a café table or reception desk. We start by asking where the light becomes a problem, when it happens and what you want people to be able to see.

topics.title: Offices and meeting rooms
topics.text: Desk positions, computer screens and meeting spaces all affect the choice. We can discuss how much daylight to keep, where glare is distracting and which windows need more privacy.

topics.title: Restaurants and cafés
topics.text: Consider the tables closest to the glass and how the sun moves during service. A treatment should address the light at those tables while fitting the atmosphere you want customers to enjoy.

topics.title: Shops and street-facing spaces
topics.text: A storefront view and a private workspace can have different needs. Tell us where visibility is welcome and where people need more coverage, so we can compare the options window by window.

feature.heading: Compare the view, coverage and finish together.
paragraphs: Solar screen shades can reduce glare while keeping a daytime view outside. A lit room may be visible from outside after dark, even when the shades are down.
Tell us when you need privacy and how much daylight you’d like to keep. We can compare more opaque roller fabrics or an additional layer where a screen shade alone won’t give enough coverage.
We can compare colors and textures with your flooring, walls and furnishings so the shades fit the room.

questions_heading: Questions about commercial blinds and shades

faqs.question: Can you help with a small office or just a few windows?
faqs.answer: Yes. You don’t need a whole-building project to start a conversation. Tell us about the room, the number of windows and what you want to improve, and we’ll discuss suitable options.

faqs.question: Can I reduce glare and still see outside?
faqs.answer: Solar screen shades can reduce glare while keeping a daytime view outside. We’ll help you compare fabrics for the view and level of glare control you want. They may still leave a lit room visible from outside after dark.

faqs.question: Can commercial shades be motorized?
faqs.answer: Compatible products can use motorized controls. We can discuss individual shades or groups, control and hub setup, and any power requirements. The available options depend on the treatment and system you choose.

faqs.question: Do you handle measuring and installation?
faqs.answer: We handle the measuring and installation, including the mounting details. If you choose motorized shades, we set up the compatible controls as well.

faqs.question: Can you come to my home or business?
faqs.answer: You can schedule a consultation for a commercial or residential space. We’ll meet you there, look at the windows and talk through what you have in mind. Photos are welcome if you’d like to send them ahead of the visit.

contact_heading: Tell us what the windows need to do.
contact_text: Schedule a consultation at your business, and we’ll look at the windows and talk through the options with you. You can also call John to discuss your project or arrange an appointment at our Woodland Hills showroom.

details.heading: Bring the product and installation details together.

items.heading: Measuring and fit.
paragraphs: Window dimensions are part of the picture. We also consider mounting depth, surrounding trim and the room needed for the treatment to move. These details help shape the product choice and installation plan.

items.heading: Controls people can use.
paragraphs: Think about who adjusts the shades and how often. We can discuss manual operation and compatible motorized controls for individual shades or groups, including the setup and power requirements of the chosen system.

items.heading: Scope, budget and timing.
paragraphs: A few office windows and a restaurant with several banks of glass involve different work. Tell us about your priorities, budget and any dates you’re working toward. We’ll discuss product availability and installation arrangements for your project.

story.heading: John’s commercial work.
paragraphs: John has supplied mesh solar shades for Western Bagel stores in the Valley, where the aim was to cut glare while keeping a view through the windows. His commercial experience also includes window covering work for The Izaka-ya by Katsu-ya.

name: Upholstery
title: Furniture Upholstery in Woodland Hills | John Crawford
description: Furniture reupholstery in Woodland Hills. Compare fabrics for a sofa or chair, discuss possible changes and get a quote based on your piece and specialist assessment.
heading: Furniture upholstery in Woodland Hills
intro: If you love a chair or have a sofa that fits your room just right, it may be worth reupholstering. We help you compare fabrics and work with an upholstery specialist to price the changes you have in mind.

overview.heading: Keep what you love about the piece.
paragraphs: The reason to reupholster is often something a replacement would be hard to offer: a familiar seat, a well-made frame or dimensions chosen for a particular room. New fabric can change the appearance while giving you a way to keep those qualities.

John is straightforward about the cost. Reupholstery can cost as much as new furniture, or more. We discuss that early, then look at the condition of the piece, the work you have in mind and what makes it worth keeping to you.

topics.title: A piece with a history
topics.text: A family chair or a sofa you’ve lived with for years can have value beyond its purchase price. Tell us what you want to preserve and what you’d like to change.

topics.title: A size that fits your room
topics.text: A custom sofa or sectional may work in a corner or layout that is difficult to furnish again. Its proportions can be a good reason to explore new upholstery.

topics.title: A frame worth considering
topics.text: A sound frame may be worth keeping even when the fabric is worn. Our upholstery specialist can assess its condition and the work needed.

feature.heading: From the first photos to your upholstery quote.
paragraphs: Start by showing us the furniture and telling us what you have in mind. Photos of the whole piece and any worn areas help us understand its shape and condition. It’s also useful to know what you like about it and your general budget.

From there, we can arrange a visit with fabric samples, take measurements and photograph the details. Seeing the furniture in its room helps with decisions about color, pattern and how the new fabric will relate to the rest of the space.

John shares the photos, measurements and proposed work with an upholstery specialist. Once the specialist has assessed the project, we prepare a quote for you to consider. You can weigh the work and cost against buying a different piece.
checklist: Photos of the whole piece and any areas of wear
What you like about the furniture and what you want to change
Ideas for fabric, color or pattern, if you have them
The furniture’s location and your general budget

faqs.question: Is reupholstery less expensive than buying new furniture?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. It can cost as much as a new piece or more. The frame, custom size, comfort or sentimental value may make the work worthwhile. A quote lets you compare the cost with the reasons you want to keep the furniture.

faqs.question: Can you bring fabric samples to my home?
faqs.answer: Yes. As part of the upholstery process, we can arrange a visit with samples, take photos and measure the furniture. Start by calling or emailing a few photos so we can talk about the piece and your plans.

faqs.question: Can the shape of a sofa or chair be changed?
faqs.answer: Some changes may be possible, such as adjusting an arm or the appearance of a back. The upholstery specialist needs to assess the frame and proposed work before we can confirm what is suitable.

faqs.question: Who carries out the upholstery work?
faqs.answer: John works with an upholstery specialist who carries out the reupholstery. We help you choose the fabric and handle the measurements, photos and quote.

faqs.question: Do I need to know which fabric I want before contacting you?
faqs.answer: No. You can start with the furniture and an idea of how you’d like the room to feel. Inspiration photos are helpful if you have them, and we can compare samples together.

contact_heading: Let’s talk about the furniture you want to keep.
contact_text: Email a few photos or call John to describe the piece, what you like about it and what you’d change. We help customers in Woodland Hills, Los Angeles and nearby Valley communities explore their upholstery options. Showroom visits are by appointment.

related.text: Drapery and fabric options for your windows

details.heading: Choose the fabric for the way you live.

items.heading: Color in your room.
paragraphs: Compare samples beside your flooring, walls and the furniture you plan to keep. A color that looks appealing on its own may feel different across a large sofa or next to a patterned rug.

items.heading: Pattern and texture.
paragraphs: A plain fabric, a visible weave and a bold pattern give the same piece very different looks. We can talk through how you want the furniture to sit within the room, whether it should be a focal point or blend into the surroundings.

items.heading: Everyday use.
paragraphs: Tell us how the furniture gets used, whether it’s a family sofa or a chair saved for guests. We’ll go through fabric samples with you and explain the care each one needs.

story.heading: A different shape may be possible, too.
paragraphs: John has worked with an upholstery specialist to reshape arms or square off a back for a more contemporary look. The options depend on the frame and construction. Share your ideas and we’ll ask the specialist what would work for your piece.
